texts.title: The Legend of Lake Toba
texts.purpose: To entertain the readers and convey a moral value about keeping promises and controlling anger.
evidences: Toba promised never to reveal his wife's secret origin as a fish.
When Toba broke his promise in anger, heavy rain flooded the valley and formed Lake Toba.

sentences: Once upon a time, a hardworking young farmer named Toba lived alone near a clear river in North Sumatra.
One afternoon, he caught a gleaming golden fish that magically transformed into a kind and graceful woman.
She agreed to marry him on one strict condition: he must never tell anyone that she came from a fish.
Years later, they had a lively son named Samosir who often played instead of helping his parents.
One hot day, Samosir ate his father's lunch on the way to the rice field because he felt hungry.
Exhausted and furious, Toba shouted at the boy and called him the son of a fish.
Hearing that forbidden secret, the mother realized that Toba had forgotten his sacred promise in a moment of anger.
She told Samosir to climb the highest hill while dark clouds suddenly gathered and rain poured nonstop for days.
Water filled the entire valley until it became a vast lake, and the woman returned to the water.
Today, people know the wide water as Lake Toba and the island in its center as Samosir Island, reminding everyone to keep their promises.

texts.title: Malin Kundang
texts.purpose: To amuse readers with a folktale and teach respect and gratitude toward parents.
evidences: Malin's mother worked tirelessly and prayed every day for her son's safe return.
Because Malin felt ashamed and denied his poor mother, his arrogance led to his tragic stone curse.

sentences: Long ago, in a quiet coastal village in West Sumatra, a poor widow named Mande Rubayah lived with her brave son, Malin Kundang.
Determined to change their fate, Malin sailed away on a merchant ship to seek a better fortune.
After many years of hard work, Malin became a wealthy ship captain and married a noblewoman.
When his grand ship anchored at his hometown, his elderly mother ran joyfully to embrace him.
Ashamed of her worn clothes in front of his wife, Malin pushed her away and claimed he did not know her.
His mother felt deeply heartbroken because wealth had blinded her beloved son from recognizing the person who raised him.
With trembling tears, she prayed to God for justice, and a fierce storm immediately struck Malin's ship.
Lightning hit the deck, and Malin Kundang knelt on the shore before turning into stone.
The stone figure on Air Manis Beach still stands as a timeless lesson to honor and love our parents.

texts.title: Sangkuriang
texts.purpose: To entertain readers with the origin story of Mount Tangkuban Perahu and remind us about honesty and patience.
evidences: Dayang Sumbi asked for a lake and a giant boat in one night to prevent a forbidden marriage.
Sangkuriang kicked the unfinished boat in rage, forming the upturned-boat shape of Mount Tangkuban Perahu.

sentences: In ancient West Java lived Dayang Sumbi, a clever princess, and her loyal dog Tumang, who was actually a cursed deity.
Her young son Sangkuriang grew up as a skilled hunter without knowing Tumang was his father.
One day, Sangkuriang failed to catch any deer and killed Tumang in frustration, causing Dayang Sumbi to banish him in sorrow.
Years later, the grown Sangkuriang returned, did not recognize his mother, and fell in love with her.
To stop the marriage, Dayang Sumbi challenged him to dam the Citarum River and build a giant boat before dawn.
Sangkuriang summoned forest spirits and nearly finished the task, so Dayang Sumbi waved a bright silk cloth to make the sky look like sunrise.
Hearing the roosters crow early, the spirits fled and left the boat incomplete.
Furious at his failure, Sangkuriang kicked the huge boat upside down until it became Mount Tangkuban Perahu.
The mountain near Bandung still resembles an overturned boat, reminding people that anger never solves a problem.

texts.title: The Clever Mouse Deer and the Crocodile
texts.purpose: To entertain readers with animal characters and show that intelligence can overcome brute strength.
evidences: The mouse deer tricked the crocodiles into lining up across the river under the excuse of counting them for a royal feast.
Instead of fighting the strong crocodiles physically, the small mouse deer used quick thinking to cross safely.

sentences: One sunny morning, a small mouse deer named Kancil felt hungry while standing beside a wide, deep river.
Across the water grew tall trees loaded with sweet, ripe mangoes, yet dangerous crocodiles guarded the stream.
Suddenly, the largest crocodile snapped his jaws near the bank and threatened to eat Kancil for breakfast.
Kancil realized he could neither swim faster than the reptiles nor defeat their sharp teeth by force.
Thinking quickly, Kancil announced that the Forest King wanted to invite all crocodiles to a grand feast if they lined up to be counted.
Eager for free food, the crocodiles formed a neat bridge from one bank to the other.
Kancil hopped lightly across their backs while counting aloud, then leaped safely onto the mango shore.
The embarrassed crocodiles learned that calm thinking is far stronger than empty boasting.

texts.title: The Proud Peacock and the Wise Owl
texts.purpose: To amuse readers and remind them that true worth comes from kindness and usefulness rather than appearance.
evidences: The peacock mocked the plain brown feathers of the owl in front of the forest birds.
When night fell and a lost fawn needed help, the owl's sharp night vision saved the day while the peacock's bright feathers could not.

sentences: In a bright green forest lived a peacock who spent every morning admiring his sparkling blue-and-gold feathers in a pond.
On a high oak branch nearby rested a quiet brown owl who rarely spoke during the day.
Whenever other birds gathered, the peacock spread his wide tail and mocked the owl's dull gray-brown wings.
That evening, thick fog covered the forest and a young deer lost its way near a steep cliff.
The panicked peacock realized that colorful feathers offered no light or guidance in the dark.
Without hesitating, the wise owl soared silently through the mist, spotted the safe path with her keen night eyes, and guided the fawn home.
The next morning, the humbled peacock bowed politely to the owl, having learned that character shines brighter than beauty.

texts.title: The Little Ant and the Golden Grain
texts.purpose: To entertain young readers and teach the value of teamwork, perseverance, and sharing.
evidences: Pip the ant could not lift the heavy golden wheat grain alone on the windy path.
By inviting his colony and sharing the food together, they moved the grain safely before the rain.

sentences: At the edge of a golden meadow, a tiny ant named Pip searched diligently for food before the rainy season arrived.
Under a clover leaf, he discovered a plump golden grain of wheat that smelled delicious.
Pip pushed and pulled with all his strength, but the heavy grain barely moved an inch.
Meanwhile, dark rain clouds rolled across the sky and a greedy beetle laughed at Pip's struggle.
Instead of giving up, Pip hurried back to the anthill and called twelve friends to help him.
Working in rhythm, the ants lifted the golden grain together and carried it inside their dry tunnel just as the first raindrops fell.
Every ant enjoyed a warm meal that night, proving that small hands united can move great burdens.

factOpinionItems.text: In 'The Legend of Lake Toba', Toba shouted at Samosir and called him the son of a fish.
factOpinionItems.reason: Ini adalah peristiwa eksplisit yang tertulis langsung di dalam teks cerita.

factOpinionItems.text: Toba is the worst father in Indonesian folklore because he lost his temper once.
factOpinionItems.reason: Kata 'the worst' adalah penilaian subjektif pembaca, bukan fakta teks.

factOpinionItems.text: Malin Kundang sailed away on a merchant ship from a coastal village in West Sumatra.
factOpinionItems.reason: Detail latar dan tindakan ini tertulis jelas pada bagian Orientation.

factOpinionItems.text: The story of Malin Kundang is much more exciting than Sangkuriang.
factOpinionItems.reason: 'much more exciting' merupakan selera atau pandangan pribadi pembaca.

factOpinionItems.text: Dayang Sumbi waved a bright silk cloth to make the sky look like sunrise.
factOpinionItems.reason: Tindakan tokoh ini tercatat secara faktual pada bagian Resolution.

factOpinionItems.text: Kancil cheated unfairly, so the crocodiles actually deserved to win.
factOpinionItems.reason: Memuat penilaian moral subjektif ('unfairly', 'deserved') yang tidak dinyatakan teks.

factOpinionItems.text: The wise owl used her keen night eyes to guide the lost fawn home through the fog.
factOpinionItems.reason: Peristiwa tersebut terjadi secara nyata dalam alur Resolution teks fabel.

factOpinionItems.text: Blue-and-gold peacock feathers are definitely the prettiest thing in any forest.
factOpinionItems.reason: Kata 'the prettiest' dan 'definitely' menunjukkan pendapat pribadi.

factOpinionItems.text: Pip called twelve friends from the anthill to help carry the golden grain.
factOpinionItems.reason: Jumlah dan kejadian ini tertulis langsung di dalam teks.

factOpinionItems.text: Fables are always easier to understand for Grade 9 students than legends.
factOpinionItems.reason: Ini adalah klaim/pendapat umum, bukan fakta dari isi cerita.

characters: A humble woodcutter and a talking white heron
A stubborn young turtle and a wise river crab
A brave village girl named Sekar and a golden deer
A clever squirrel and a boastful eagle
settings: In a misty bamboo valley in ancient Java
Along a sparkling coral bay in Eastern Indonesia
Inside an enchanted pine forest before the monsoon
Near a crystal waterfall at the foot of Mount Merapi
problems: A drought dried up the village spring after someone broke a promise
A giant storm trapped the forest animals on a tiny mud island
A greedy merchant stole the magic seed that fed the whole valley
A young hero underestimated a small friend during a race across the canyon
morals: Honesty and keeping promises protect harmony with nature.
Teamwork and humility overcome challenges that pride cannot solve.
True courage means helping others even when you feel afraid.
